title: Cartan generators and the Serre quotient
notes: Generators \(e_i,h_i,f_i\) satisfy \([e_i,f_j]=\delta_{ij}h_i\), \([h_i,e_j]=a_{ij}e_j\), \([h_i,f_j]=-a_{ij}f_j\), and commuting \(h_i\). Gelfand says \ru{Корней можно не учить}. The extra relations are written as ordinary powers, and the off-diagonal inequality is strict.
statement: For a generalized Cartan matrix \(A\), require \(a_{ii}=2\), \(a_{ij}\in\mathbb Z_{\le0}\) for \(i\ne j\), and \(a_{ij}=0\iff a_{ji}=0\). The derived Kac--Moody algebra is generated by these elements subject to the displayed brackets and \((\operatorname{ad}e_i)^{1-a_{ij}}e_j=(\operatorname{ad}f_i)^{1-a_{ij}}f_j=0\), \(i\ne j\). Root vectors are obtained from iterated Lie brackets, not associative products.
reconstruction: The generalized Cartan conditions, adjoint notation, and distinction between the derived algebra and its Cartan extension are editorial qualifications.
fate: The finite-growth construction predates the talk: \citet[Chapter II]{kac1968graded}; the standard presentation is organized in \citet[Chapter 1]{kac1983infinite}. The notebook compresses several statements into an informal uniqueness assertion.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Finite and affine types and the rank-two examples
notes: Finite-dimensionality is identified with \(A>0\); affine type with \(A\ge0\), rank \(n-1\). Rank-two examples are \(A_2,B_2,G_2\). The first affine matrix is written \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&-2\\-2&-2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), then corrected implicitly in Kirillov\textquotesingle s repetition.
statement: For an indecomposable symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix \(A\), choose positive diagonal \(D\) with \(DA\) symmetric. Finite type is equivalent to positive definiteness of \(DA\); affine type to positive semidefiniteness of corank one. The affine matrices here are \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) and \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&-4\\-1&2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).
reconstruction: Indecomposability, symmetrizability and the positive diagonal symmetrizer are added; the lower-right affine entry is emended to +2.
fate: Finite/affine classification is old material in \citet[Chapter II]{kac1968graded}; \citet[Chapter 4]{kac1983infinite} gives the generalized Cartan formulation. Positivity of a nonsymmetric matrix requires interpretation.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: The Heisenberg central extension of a symplectic space
notes: \(E\oplus\mathbb R\mathbf1\), with \([x,y]=\langle x,y\rangle\mathbf1\), is introduced as the Heisenberg algebra.
statement: If \((E,\omega)\) is a real symplectic vector space, define \([(x,a),(y,b)]=(0,\omega(x,y))\). Bilinearity, antisymmetry and centrality give a Lie algebra; for finite-dimensional nondegenerate \(E\) its center is exactly \(\mathbb R\mathbf1\).
reconstruction: Nondegeneracy and the finite-dimensional qualification for the center are explicit here.
fate: This is the standard central-extension model underlying the oscillator realization in \citet[pp.~43--53]{lepowskywilson1978construction}; the definition itself needs no conjectural step.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Loop realization and the sign of the central cocycle
notes: The notes use \([A,B]=AB-BA+\operatorname{Res}\operatorname{tr}(A\,dB)\mathbf1\), with \(e_1=E_{12}\), \(f_1=E_{21}\), \(e_2=tE_{21}\), \(f_2=t^{-1}E_{12}\), and \(h_2=-h_1+\mathbf1\).
statement: On \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C[t,t^{-1}])\oplus\mathbb C K\), the cocycle \(\operatorname{Res}\operatorname{tr}((dA)B)\) yields \([e_2,f_2]=-h_1+K\). Using \(\operatorname{Res}\operatorname{tr}(A\,dB)\) instead yields \(-h_1-K\). Either convention defines the central extension, but the displayed bracket and \(h_2\) must agree.
reconstruction: The residue convention is fixed explicitly; replacing the cocycle sign is an emendation, not a different historical claim.
fate: This is the loop realization of the affine algebra, already used in the construction summarized by \citet{lepowskywilson1978construction}; see also \citet[Chapter 7]{kac1983infinite}. The sign discrepancy is checked directly by differentiating \(t^{-1}\).
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Root monomials and the proposal to make paths continuous
notes: Weights count occurrences of the \(e_j\) in a monomial. A staircase path is drawn, followed by \ru{как сделать, чтобы пути были непрерывны?}
statement: A Lie word has multidegree given by its generator multiplicities. The question about continuous paths specifies neither a topology, a limiting parameter, nor which algebraic operations the path model must preserve; no unique mathematical problem can be recovered.
reconstruction: Only the multigrading is definite. No Littelmann-path or stochastic-path theorem is imported.
fate: Comparison with the published affine construction and Kac\textquotesingle s representation framework yields no exact target. Later path models cannot be identified with this sentence merely from the word ``paths\textquotesingle\textquotesingle.

title: The basic highest-weight module
notes: A cyclic vector satisfies \(e_1v_0=e_2v_0=0\), \(h_1v_0=0\), \(h_2v_0=v_0\). Its space is \(\mathbb C[x_1,x_3,x_5,\ldots]\).
statement: For the affine algebra with \(K=h_1+h_2\), the irreducible integrable highest-weight module of weight \(\Lambda\) with \(\Lambda(h_1)=0\), \(\Lambda(h_2)=1\) has level one and the principal bosonic realization on the polynomial algebra in positive odd variables. The Verma module with these highest weights must first be quotiented by its maximal proper submodule.
reconstruction: Irreducibility, integrability, level and the quotient qualification make the notebook	extquotesingle s ``most economical	extquotesingle	extquotesingle precise.
fate: Exactly the odd-variable realization is identified by the original abstract of \citet{lepowskywilson1978construction}, published August 1978. The distinction between Verma and irreducible integrable modules is essential.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Nonconjugate loop Cartans and the square-root obstruction
notes: After quotienting by the center, diagonal loops and matrices \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&f(t)\\tf(t)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) form nonconjugate commutative subalgebras. Pointwise diagonalization is possible, but continuous diagonalization is not.
statement: For \(t\in S^1\), \(B(t)=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\t&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) has distinct eigenvalues \(\pm\sqrt t\). A continuous periodic diagonalization with labeled diagonal entries would give a continuous square root of \(t\), impossible since its winding number would be one half. Over \(\mathbb C[t,t^{-1}]\) this likewise obstructs conjugation to the split diagonal Cartan.
reconstruction: The domain S1, complex coefficient field, and nonvanishing choice f=1 are specified; no obstruction is claimed on a simply connected arc.
fate: The principal Heisenberg in \citet{lepowskywilson1978construction} implements this distinction. The winding-number explanation supplied here is an elementary reconstruction of the specific notebook example.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Principal Heisenberg modes and the Fock representation
notes: \(B_{2k+1}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&t^k\\t^{k+1}&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), with \([B_{2k+1},B_{2l+1}]=\delta(k+l)(2l+1)\mathbf1\), is followed by multiplication/differentiation operators and an irreducibility assertion.

title: Exponential modes realize the remaining affine generators
notes: The notes form \(L=e^{\sum x_k}e^{4\sum\partial_{x_k}}=\sum L_m\), with weighted homogeneous components, and express \(C_{2k+1}\) and \(H_{2k}\) through them.
statement: The principal realization extends the Heisenberg action on \(\mathbb C[x_1,x_3,\ldots]\) to the basic affine module using coefficients of a normally ordered formal exponential field. Each coefficient acts on a polynomial through finitely many derivative terms; the multiplication part is interpreted in the graded completion. The coefficients and grading must be chosen together to satisfy the affine brackets.

title: Lorentzian area action and its sign
notes: The target metric is \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,\ldots,-1)\), while the integrand is \(\sqrt{\dot X^2(X^{\prime})^2-(\dot X\cdot X^{\prime})^2}\).
statement: For a timelike immersed worldsheet with induced metric \(h_{ab}=\partial_aX\cdot\partial_bX\), a real action is \(S=-T\int\sqrt{-\det h}\,d\tau\,d\sigma=-T\int\sqrt{(\dot X\cdot X^{\prime})^2-\dot X^2(X^{\prime})^2}\,d\tau\,d\sigma\), \(T>0\). Degenerate worldsheets need separate treatment.
reconstruction: The tension, timelike immersion and real square-root convention are supplied.
fate: This is established string mechanics; \citet[Section1.2]{tong2009string} supplies an explicitly normalized reference. The square-root sign follows directly from Lorentzian signature.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Singular Legendre transform and first-class constraints
notes: The canonical Hamiltonian vanishes. Constraints are first \(p^2-(X^{\prime})^2=0,\ p\cdot X^{\prime}=0\), then \((p\pm X^{\prime})^2=0\); a Hamiltonian is formed from arbitrary multipliers.
statement: For the Lorentzian area action, \(p^2+T^2(X^{\prime})^2=0\) and \(p\cdot X^{\prime}=0\). The canonical Hamiltonian vanishes by degree-one velocity homogeneity. The total Hamiltonian is a linear combination of these first-class constraints; lapse and shift encode worldsheet reparametrization.
reconstruction: Tension T is restored and the conflicting sign is repaired.
fate: Dirac developed the framework in August1949 lectures and \citet[Sections2--4]{dirac1950generalized}. The string specialization is checked by differentiating the action.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Two classical Witt algebras and Fourier conventions
notes: Modes of \((p+X^{\prime})^2\) and \((p-X^{\prime})^2\) close as commuting Witt algebras. \(X\) and \(p\) use opposite Fourier signs, but their mode bracket uses \(\delta_{n+m,0}\).
statement: The smeared chiral constraints have the brackets of vector fields on \(S^1\), with opposite orientation conventions for the chiralities and zero mixed bracket. If \(X=\sum x_ne^{in\sigma}\), \(p=\sum p_me^{-im\sigma}\), normalization aside \(\{x_n,p_m\}=\delta_{nm}\); same-sign expansions give \(\delta_{n+m,0}\).
reconstruction: The algebraic claim and the inconsistent Fourier convention are separated; factors of \(2\pi\) depend on normalization.
fate: This is the classical constraint calculation underlying \citet[Sections1.4 and2.1]{tong2009string}. Fourier orthogonality gives the delta correction. First-class closure also proves preservation of the constraints by multiplier evolution.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Oscillators, Fock space and the Virasoro central term
notes: Oscillators combine \(p_n,x_n\), a vacuum is annihilated for \(n\ge0\), and quadratic modes acquire \(D(n^3-n)/12\). Individual Fourier modes are called Hermitian.
statement: Normalize \([\alpha_m^\mu,\alpha_n^\nu]=m\eta^{\mu\nu}\delta_{m+n,0}\), \((\alpha_n^\mu)^\dagger=\alpha_{-n}^\mu\), \(\alpha_n|0;p\rangle=0\) for \(n>0\), and \(L_n=\tfrac12\sum_m:\alpha_{n-m}\cdot\alpha_m:\). On finite excitations, \([L_m,L_n]=(m-n)L_{m+n}+\tfrac D{12}(m^3-m)\delta_{m+n,0}\). The zero mode is momentum, not an oscillator annihilator.
reconstruction: A common algebraic domain, Minkowski contraction, one-half factor and zero-mode sector are explicit.
fate: The oscillator construction predates1982; \citet[Section2.1]{tong2009string} makes conventions explicit. Reality, mode factors and the zero-mode qualification are distinct defects.

title: Incompatibility of all quantum Virasoro constraints
notes: The notes say that all \(L_n\Psi=0\) are incompatible with the central term.
statement: If \(c\ne0\) and every \(L_n v=0\) on a common invariant domain, then \(0=[L_2,L_{-2}]v=(4L_0+c/2)v=(c/2)v\), hence \(v=0\). This is a statement before canceling matter and ghost central charges.
reconstruction: The elementary proof and the distinction from the total anomaly-free BRST complex are editorial.
fate: The claim follows immediately from the known Virasoro relation; \citet[Section2.1.2]{tong2009string} discusses the physical constraint prescription.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Half-constraints and physical matrix elements
notes: Only \(L_n\Psi=0\) for \(n\ge0\) are imposed; every constraint is then said to have vanishing physical matrix elements.
statement: With \(L_n^\dagger=L_{-n}\), \(L_n v=0\) for \(n>0\) and \((L_0-a)v=0\) imply \(\langle u,L_nv\rangle=0\) for \(n\ne0\) and \(\langle u,(L_0-a)v\rangle=0\) between physical vectors. These conditions alone prove neither positivity nor consistency in arbitrary dimension.
reconstruction: The intercept and limits of the matrix-element conclusion are restored.
fate: This is the old covariant prescription with the intercept suppressed; see \citet[Section2.1.2]{tong2009string}. Conjugation proves the negative-mode assertion.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Cyclic iterated integrals as classical string observables
notes: Ordered products of \(y^\mu=p^\mu+iX^{\prime\mu}\) are integrated over cyclically ordered points. Their \(Q\)s are said to commute with constraints and momentum; the classical bracket has length \(n+m-2\).
statement: For a closed classical string put \(u_\pm=p\pm TX^{\prime}\). Sum ordered iterated integrals over cyclic permutations of tensor indices. These charges are independent of the starting point, invariant under orientation-preserving reparametrizations and conserved on shell. Their span, shuffle multiplication and induced Poisson bracket form a Poisson algebra; the bracket contracts one index from each word.
reconstruction: The real Lorentzian currents replace the unexplained printed \(i\). The length rule is schematic: coefficients, contractions and shuffle relations remain necessary.
fate: This matches the Pohlmeyer--Rehren construction, explicitly given in \citet[Equations1.1--1.2 and Section2]{bahnsmeinecke2011string}. Its first cited publication is Pohlmeyer1982; accessible evidence did not date circulation before this September talk. Later algebraic development is by others, hence B.
present_status: As of November 2026: the classical cyclic-charge Poisson algebra is established.

title: Normal ordering does not preserve all charge relations
notes: After adding normal-ordering colons, the notes assert \([Q,L_n]=0\).
statement: Expand classical charges in oscillators and normally order formally. Their constraint commutators and defining relations still require verification. Naive canonical normal ordering does not in general yield the invariant algebra with only observable quantum corrections.
reconstruction: The universal quantum assertion is separated from classical invariance and alternative quantizations.
fate: \citet[Sections4--5]{bahns2004string} finds anomalous terms which cannot be removed by changing target dimension. This negative result concerns that prescription, not every deformation quantization.
present_status: As of November 2026: the unqualified canonical normal-ordering assertion fails.

title: The quantum algebra of cyclic charges
notes: Zamolodchikov asks for the mutual commutation relations of the \(Q\)s, after stating the classical length rule.
statement: For the cyclic-charge Poisson algebra \(\mathfrak h\), construct an associative formal deformation over \(\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\) with zeroth product the shuffle product and first commutator \(i\hbar\{\, ,\,\}\), and describe its quantum relations. The notes impose no Hilbert-space representation requirement.
reconstruction: Formal deformation and the semiclassical condition specify the algebraic question. Preferred explicit presentations and positive representations are stronger requirements.
fate: \citet[Theorem1.1]{enriquezhalbout2010quantization}, circulated2008 and published2010, constructs quasi-Lie-bialgebra quantization. \citet[Proposition15 and p.~20]{bahnsmeinecke2011string} explicitly deduces existence for \(\mathfrak h\) without quadratic generation. This substantial algebraic answer does not validate the notebook operators.
present_status: As of November 2026: abstract formal quantization exists; the question is not catalogued as an open existence problem.

title: Completeness of invariant charges
notes: The continuation calls \(\{Q\}\) a complete set of invariants commuting with \(P^\mu\).
statement: Completeness requires a specified class of worldsheets and an equivalence by translations and reparametrization. It does not assert free algebraic independence or generation of every momentum-commuting function without regularity restrictions.
reconstruction: Completeness is interpreted geometrically, without promoting the abbreviated assertion to an unrestricted theorem.

title: Perturbative renormalizability after gauging
notes: The statement attributed to 't Hooft says that if \(L\) is renormalizable, its localization is also renormalizable.
statement: In four dimensions, Yang--Mills theories with compact gauge group and power-counting renormalizable matter interactions admit perturbative renormalization compatible with gauge identities when gauge anomalies cancel. Spontaneous breaking by scalar vacuum expectation values does not by itself destroy this property. Gauging an arbitrary global symmetry without anomaly checks is not a valid universal implication.
reconstruction: Dimension, interaction degree, anomaly cancellation and perturbative scope are supplied.
fate: \citet[Introduction and Sections2--5]{thooft1971massive} treats the gauge identities and explicit scalar models in1971. This is perturbative renormalizability, not construction of a nonperturbative continuum probability measure.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Vacuum manifold and symmetry breaking
notes: Constant minimizers of \(U\) form \(\mathcal R\). For \(U(\phi)=\lambda(|\phi|^2-a^2)^2\), the vacuum set is a sphere; \(H_\phi\) is the subgroup fixing a vacuum.
statement: For \(\lambda>0,a>0\) and \(\phi\in\mathbb R^n\), the minima are \(S^{n-1}_a\). When a compact group \(G\) acts transitively on a vacuum component, it is \(G/H_\phi\). This vacuum orbit is a space of Higgs field values; gauge-equivalent constant configurations need not be distinct physical vacua.
reconstruction: Positivity, transitivity, vacuum component and gauge-equivalence distinctions are made explicit.
fate: This is standard Higgs-model geometry; \citet[Section3]{thooft1971massive} explicitly analyzes the scalar minimum and residual gauge symmetry.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Grand unification and the affine-group proposal
notes: The low-energy group is \(SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)\); candidates for a larger group include \(SU(5),SO(10),E_8\). Gelfand proposes an affine group, emphasizing finite rank and an invariant form.
statement: An embedding of the indicated Lie algebra into a larger gauge algebra is only group-theoretic input. A unification model additionally requires matter representations, symmetry-breaking fields, interactions and anomaly conditions. The affine suggestion specifies none of these and therefore does not define a unique field theory or existence problem.
fate: The finite-group mirror construction subsequently published by \citet{fateevfrolovschwarz1982mirror} is an identifiable nearby model, not a realization of the unspecified affine proposal. No exact affine-model target was found in the author bibliography or prior occurrence index.
present_status: As of November 2026: the proposal remains underdetermined; it is not evidence of an unsolved general unification theorem.

title: Monopole sectors from the sphere at spatial infinity
notes: Finite-energy fields on \(\mathbb R^3\) approach \(\mathcal R\) at infinity, defining \(S^2\to\mathcal R\), hence an element of \(\pi_2(\mathcal R)\) and monopoles.
statement: For a Higgs model with positive potential vanishing exactly on a vacuum manifold, impose asymptotic boundary conditions ensuring that the normalized Higgs field extends continuously to the sphere at infinity. Its homotopy class lies in \(\pi_2(\mathcal R)\). Nontrivial classes distinguish sectors but do not alone prove that a finite-energy minimizing solution exists in every class.

present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Strings and fundamental-group sectors
notes: A string is independent of the longitudinal coordinate and has finite energy per unit length. A linking circle maps to \(\mathcal R\); stability is followed by a question mark.
statement: For a translationally invariant configuration on \(\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R\), require \(\int_{\mathbb R^2}\mathcal E\,dx\,dy<\infty\) and a limiting Higgs map \(S^1_\infty\to\mathcal R\). Its class in \(\pi_1(\mathcal R)\) obstructs deformation to vacuum through admissible finite-energy configurations. This is topological stability, not a proof of spectral, nonlinear or quantum stability.
reconstruction: Boundary conditions, energy per unit length and the meaning of stability are separated.

present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Charge-reversing holonomy and the missing disconnected stabilizer
notes: If an element \(\alpha\in\widetilde G\) conjugates the electromagnetic \(U(1)\) by inversion, the notes assert existence of a topologically nontrivial charge-reversing string. The unbroken group is written \(K\times U(1)\).
statement: Let \(\widetilde G\) be simply connected and \(H\) its unbroken subgroup. A string class corresponds to a component of \(H\), since \(\pi_1(\widetilde G/H)\cong\pi_0(H)\). A representative holonomy \(\alpha\in H\) can reverse charge if \(\alpha Q\alpha^{-1}=-Q\). Merely finding \(\alpha\) in \(\widetilde G\) is insufficient: connected \(H\) gives no such fundamental-group string. Field-equation existence needs model-specific energy analysis.
reconstruction: The homotopy-sequence calculation and the condition alpha in H outside its identity component repair the stated criterion.
fate: The mechanism was announced in \citet{schwarz1981nonlocal}; \citet{schwarz1982charge} explicitly assumes a disconnected unbroken subgroup. The1981 announcement makes this E despite the later detailed paper.
present_status: As of November 2026: the Alice-string mechanism is established; the printed sufficient condition is incomplete.

title: Ordinary-to-mirror particle transport around a string
notes: There are unified models containing mirror particles and strings around which a particle becomes its mirror partner. The two sectors interact weakly through heavy bosons and share gravity; mirror particles are not antiparticles.
statement: Choose a gauge model whose disconnected residual symmetry exchanges two matter sectors. Holonomy in that component transports a state in one sector to its mirror partner. Decoupling of local nongravitational interactions at low energy is a separate statement about heavy mediator masses and couplings, not a consequence of topology alone.
reconstruction: Holonomy exchange and low-energy coupling suppression are distinct assumptions.
fate: \citet[pp.~427--432]{fateevfrolovschwarz1982mirror} publishes the specific model in December1982, after this talk, and its abstract states precisely the sector exchange. An earlier preprint date was not verified. Classification A records the speaker's subsequent publication, with abstract-level verification.
present_status: As of November 2026: the proposed gauge-theory mechanism was published; this does not establish the existence of mirror matter in nature.

title: Quantum stability of the proposed strings
notes: \ru{Неясно, сущ. ли квантово стабильные нити}; classical stability is asserted.
statement: A quantum-stability question must specify the Lagrangian, coupling regime, boundary sector and whether stability means an exact conserved topological charge, absence of tunneling, a positive fluctuation spectrum or a lifetime. The notes do not select one meaning or one model.
fate: The Schwarz and Fateev--Frolov--Schwarz publications identify nearby classical constructions; their accessible abstracts do not supply the missing quantum target. No exact quantum-stability theorem can responsibly be assigned to this sentence.
present_status: As of November 2026: underdetermined, rather than a newly formulated universal open problem.

title: Mirror-photon visibility and the quasar anecdote
notes: The diagram suggests that a string crossing a line of sight can turn photons into mirror photons. Khlopov mentions a preprint about a quasar whose luminosity changed sharply over a century.
statement: A sector-exchanging holonomy can change which asymptotic gauge field a transported state couples to. Predicting an observed light curve requires an explicit spacetime string configuration, propagation and source model. The notebook gives no quasar name, preprint author list or measurable parameters.
fate: The mirror-particle paper identifies the particle-transport mechanism only. The observational anecdote could not be uniquely identified from the named author and sparse description; it is not treated as experimental confirmation.

title: Fixed-length random rods and their endpoint distribution
notes: \(G_N(R)=\int\prod d n_i\,\delta(\sum n_i-R/\Delta)\); Fourier transformation gives \(C(p,\Delta)^N\), and a recurrence is requested.
statement: With normalized rotation-invariant measure \(\sigma\) on \(S^{d-1}\), the endpoint density is \(p_N(R)=\int\delta(R-\Delta\sum n_i)\prod d\sigma(n_i)=\Delta^{-d}G_N(R)\). It satisfies \(p_{N+1}(R)=\int p_N(R-\Delta n)d\sigma(n)\) and \(\widehat p_N=C^N\), where \(C=\int e^{i\Delta p\cdot n}d\sigma(n)\). For \(d\ge2\), \(C=\Gamma(d/2)(2/(\Delta|p|))^{d/2-1}J_{d/2-1}(\Delta|p|)\), continuously extended at zero.
reconstruction: Probability normalization, the missing delta-function Jacobian and the recurrence are supplied.
fate: This is a direct finite-dimensional derivation of the notebook regularization. Its historical role is the path analogue of \citet[Equations~(1)--(2)]{polyakov1981quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Diffusive scaling, mass tuning and the quadratic momentum term
notes: Equations (19)--(20) sum the step characteristic function and then use an exponent \(a+b\vec p-m\), before obtaining a propagator \(1/(p^2+m_R^2)\).
statement: For isotropic unit steps, \(C(p,\Delta)=1-\Delta^2|p|^2/(2d)+O(\Delta^4|p|^4)\). Put \(a_\Delta=\Delta^2/(2d)\) and choose per-step weight \(q_\Delta=1-m_R^2a_\Delta+o(a_\Delta)\). Then \(a_\Delta\sum_{N\ge0}(q_\Delta C)^N\to(m_R^2+|p|^2)^{-1}\) for \(m_R>0\). Unnormalized step measures require additional entropy compensation in \(q_\Delta\).
reconstruction: A definite scaling limit replaces the undefined constants a,b and clarifies mass renormalization.
fate: The limit follows by expansion and a geometric series, within the path framework of \citet{polyakov1981quantum}. A linear isotropic momentum term cannot produce it.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Gaussian increments, Wiener measure and proper time
notes: The rods become springs, their lengths are called Gaussian, and a formal integral \(e^{-\frac12\int\dot X^2}\) over paths is called Wiener measure.
statement: Gaussian displacement vectors with covariance \(\Delta I\), each normalized by \((2\pi\Delta)^{-d/2}\), converge to Brownian motion with generator \(\tfrac12\Delta_x\). The endpoint heat kernel has Fourier multiplier \(e^{-\tau|p|^2/2}\). Integrating against \(e^{-a\tau}\,d\tau\), \(a>0\), yields \((a+|p|^2/2)^{-1}\). Brownian paths have infinite ordinary arclength almost surely; the kinetic action is symbolic rather than a finite pathwise function.
reconstruction: Displacements replace Gaussian lengths; normalization, generator and the symbolic action convention are explicit.
fate: The Wiener-functional tradition precedes the seminar; \citet{kac1949distributions} is verified bibliographically only. The Gaussian convolution and Laplace transform above are checked directly. Matching the previous convention requires rescaling time and mass.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: The Euclidean massive Green function
notes: \(\widehat G(p)=z/(p^2+m^2)\), whose inverse is called a Hankel function.
statement: With Fourier inverse \((2\pi)^{-d}\int e^{ip\cdot R}\,dp\), for \(m>0\), \(R\ne0\), the kernel is \(G(R)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}(m/|R|)^{d/2-1}K_{d/2-1}(m|R|)\). A Hankel-function expression requires analytic continuation to an imaginary argument or a Lorentzian prescription; the decaying Euclidean expression uses modified Bessel \(K\).
reconstruction: The transform convention, massive regime and relation to the Hankel terminology are stated.
fate: This follows by integrating the Gaussian heat kernel in proper time, the framework associated with \citet{kac1949distributions}. The normalization and function type are an editorial calculation.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: A spring mesh gives a Gaussian field at fixed worldsheet geometry
notes: A square spring network gives \(\int DX\exp[-\tfrac12\int(\partial X)^2]\); a regular grid is said to be insufficient for general surfaces.
statement: For a fixed two-dimensional mesh and boundary conditions, a quadratic spring energy defines a finite-dimensional Gaussian measure after removing or fixing zero modes. Its continuum limit is a Gaussian free field at the chosen conformal structure. Varying embedded vertices on a fixed mesh does not by itself specify a sum over intrinsic metrics or topologies.
reconstruction: Boundary/zero-mode conditions and fixed intrinsic geometry are added.
fate: The distinction motivates \citet[Equations~(6), (14)]{polyakov1981quantum}. The notebook drawings do not define a unique discretization-independent surface measure.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Why the bosonic critical dimension is 26
notes: The fixed-metric quadratic action gives the \ru{прав. ответ} in target dimension 26.
statement: In bosonic Polyakov gauge fixing, \(D\) free scalar matter fields contribute central charge \(D\), and the reparametrization ghosts contribute \(-26\). The local Weyl anomaly cancels at \(D=26\). This does not prove convergence over topologies, absence of tachyons, or existence of an unrestricted surface probability measure.
reconstruction: The anomaly statement replaces the unqualified phrase correct answer.
fate: The coefficient is calculated in \citet[Equations~(23)--(25)]{polyakov1981quantum}, before the talk.

title: The independent-metric action and cosmological term
notes: The final integral introduces \(g_{ab}\) and \(+\lambda\int\sqrt g\) in the exponent, then says minimizing recovers the earlier equations.
statement: The classical action \(S_P=\tfrac12\int\sqrt g\,g^{ab}\partial_aX\cdot\partial_bX\), varied in \(X\) and \(g\), imposes harmonicity and vanishing stress tensor. For a nondegenerate induced metric this makes \(g\) conformal to it and recovers area. A nonzero classical cosmological term changes the trace equation: in two dimensions the kinetic stress tensor is traceless, so that term must vanish. In the formal quantum measure it is instead a cutoff-dependent counterterm.
reconstruction: The trace check explicitly separates the classical and quantum roles of lambda.
fate: \citet[Equations~(6)--(7), (14), p.~209]{polyakov1981quantum} separates these roles. Gauge volume, moduli and boundary conditions also need specification.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Parameters of regular adjoint orbits
notes: \(\Omega_c\) is parametrized by \(\ell=\operatorname{rank}G\) invariants, illustrated by \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) hyperboloids and traces of powers.
statement: For a complex semisimple algebra, invariant polynomials parametrize the adjoint quotient, and regular semisimple fibers are single complex adjoint orbits. For real groups, invariant values alone can combine several real orbits. In \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)\), the negative and positive values of the invariant quadratic form give different hyperboloid types; the two sheets need not be one orbit.
reconstruction: The field, regular semisimple restriction and real-orbit distinction are supplied.
fate: The complex-as-real scope used by \citet[Sections~1--2]{ginzburg1983integrals} is narrower than the notebook\textquotesingle s initial arbitrary Lie group. The rank-one real qualification follows directly from the adjoint quadratic form.

title: Springer incidence resolution
notes: For the unipotent variety \(N\), let \(\mathcal B\) be the Borel variety and \(\mathcal M=\{(n,B):n\in N,\ n\in B\}\); projection to \(N\) is called a desingularization.
statement: For a connected complex semisimple algebraic group in characteristic zero, \(\widetilde N=G\times^B U_B\to N\) is proper and birational, with smooth source; its fiber over \(n\) is the Borel subgroups containing \(n\). In Lie-algebra form \(G\times^B\mathfrak n_B\simeq T^*(G/B)\) resolves the nilpotent cone. Properness and birationality, not just equal dimension and generic bijectivity, belong to the resolution statement.
reconstruction: Complex algebraic hypotheses, properness and the Lie-algebra/group distinction are explicit.
fate: This is the preexisting Springer framework cited by \citet{springer1976trigonometric} and used explicitly in \citet[Section~9]{ginzburg1983integrals}. The exact earlier incidence-resolution occurrence is 1971-231.2; 1971-231.5 concerns the related Springer-fiber dimension.

title: The real cylinder-to-cone illustration
notes: The drawing maps a cylinder to a double cone by \((x,y,z)\mapsto(xz,yz,z)\), collapsing its middle circle; it is identified with the \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) example.
statement: On \(x^2+y^2=1\), this map lands in \(X^2+Y^2=Z^2\), is one-to-one away from the cone vertex, and collapses exactly \(S^1\times\{0\}\). It models the topology of the real rank-one Springer map, whose exceptional fiber is \(\mathbb{RP}^1\simeq S^1\). The complex exceptional fiber is instead \(\mathbb{CP}^1\); the real drawing is not a description of all complex algebraic data.
reconstruction: The source cylinder equation and the real versus complex interpretation are supplied.
fate: The topology is checked directly from the displayed map and the flag fiber, within the Springer framework used by \citet[Sections~3,9]{ginzburg1983integrals}.

title: Nilpotent orbital integrals from regular semisimple ones
notes: \(\psi(c)=\int_{\Omega_c}f\), with coherently chosen measures; \(\int_{\Omega_0}f=(P\psi)(0)\), \(P\) a differential operator.
statement: For a complex semisimple Lie algebra regarded as a real Lie algebra and a Schwartz test function \(f\), each nilpotent orbital integral is a constant multiple of a constant-coefficient differential operator applied at zero to the normalized Harish--Chandra orbital transform on a Cartan subalgebra. The operator polynomial is obtained from the corresponding Springer homology representation. Raw integrals in arbitrary quotient coordinates do not automatically satisfy the abbreviated identity.
reconstruction: The group class, Schwartz decay, Cartan normalization, measure constants and orbit-dependent operator are restored.
fate: \citet[Formula~(1), Sections~1--7]{ginzburg1983integrals} proves the Barbasch--Vogan conjectural formula in this scope. Presented 19 October 1982, received 23 November 1982 and published in 1983, it matches Kirillov\textquotesingle s report of another mathematician\textquotesingle s work; class B records that authorship.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identified complex-group limit formula is established; no claim about all real reductive groups is inferred.

title: Recovering the crossing value from hyperbola integrals
notes: Gelfand asks to recover \(f(0)\) from integrals over \(xy=c\), and refers to an expansion of \(\delta(xy-c)\) in the first volume of Generalized Functions.
statement: For \(f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)\), set \(I_f(c)=\int f(x,y)\delta(xy-c)\,dx\,dy\), \(c\ne0\). Then \(I_f(c)=-2f(0,0)\log|c|+O(1)\), so \(f(0,0)=\lim_{c\to0}I_f(c)/(-2\log|c|)\). This uses the delta/coarea measure, not ordinary arclength. Restricting to a single positive branch halves the leading coefficient.
reconstruction: Compact support, delta measure and the exact leading coefficient are supplied; this is an elementary reconstruction of the recorded question.
fate: The notes themselves identify the preexisting distribution-theoretic setting of \citet{gelfandshilov1964generalized}; only its bibliographic record was accessible. The stated leading term is verified here \ours by writing \(I_f(c)=\int f(x,c/x)\,dx/|x|\), splitting near zero, and estimating the smooth remainder.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Why the singular limit contains logarithms
notes: The text speaks of expanding \(\delta(xy-c)\) in powers of \(c\), then taking the hyperbola limit to obtain integrals over straight lines.
statement: At the critical level \(c=0\), the pullback distribution cannot be handled by an ordinary Taylor expansion: \(d(xy)=0\) at the crossing. Asymptotics involve logarithmic terms and finite-part distributions on the axes. Writing a finite coefficient through axis integrals requires a finite-part prescription; changing that prescription is compensated by a multiple of the point delta distribution. The coefficient of the fixed distribution family itself is not arbitrary.
reconstruction: The need for logarithmic/finite-part terms is an explicit mathematical correction, without claiming an unread full asymptotic formula.
fate: The source allusion is to \citet{gelfandshilov1964generalized}; the leading logarithm above directly rules out an unqualified power-series or finite unrenormalized limit. The exact book passage was not located.

title: Proper time and the particle Green function
notes: Equations (2)--(2\textquotesingle) replace the length-weighted sum by an integral over \(\tau>0\) and Brownian paths with kinetic term \(\frac12\int\dot x^2dt\), giving \(\tau^{-d/2}\exp[-m^2\tau-R^2/(2\tau)]\).
statement: For Brownian motion with generator \(\frac12\Delta\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), the heat kernel is \(p_\tau(R)=(2\pi\tau)^{-d/2}e^{-|R|^2/(2\tau)}\). For \(m^2>0\), its Laplace transform is the resolvent kernel of \(m^2-\frac12\Delta\), with Fourier multiplier \((m^2+|p|^2/2)^{-1}\). The length-weighted lattice sum reaches this expression only after a specified diffusive limit and mass renormalization.
reconstruction: The normalized heat kernel, generator and positive-mass hypothesis are supplied. The formula does not assign ordinary arc length to Brownian paths.
fate: This is the particle comparison underlying \citet[Eqs.~(1)--(5)]{polyakov1981quantum}; it repeats the preceding lecture in a consistent proper-time normalization.

title: Entropy subtraction and the renormalized mass
notes: The number of length-\(L\) paths is written \(f(L)\sim L^\beta e^{\varkappa L}\), with \(\varkappa\) cutoff-dependent and \(\beta\) cutoff-independent; the notes conclude \(m^2=m_0-\varkappa\).
statement: For a specified lattice-walk ensemble the exponential growth constant shifts the bare length penalty to \(m_0-\varkappa\). A Brownian continuum limit additionally rescales the number of steps as inverse step length squared and fixes the diffusion coefficient. Consequently the numerical identity \(m^2=m_0-\varkappa\) is schematic until the units of \(L\) and \(\tau\) and the cutoff scaling are specified. Polynomial exponents depend on dimension, endpoints and the walk ensemble.
reconstruction: The identification is kept as a scaling prescription. No self-avoiding-walk or arbitrary-regulator universality claim is supplied.
fate: \citet[Eqs.~(1)--(5)]{polyakov1981quantum} uses the same random-walk analogy. The entropy subtraction is standard; the notes do not state a universality theorem encompassing different path ensembles.

title: The remark about singular infinite-dimensional measures
notes: A margin says \ru{В \(\infty\)-мерном пр-ве почти \(\forall\) две меры взаимно сингулярны}.
statement: There is no specified class of measures or measure on that class, so the phrase almost every pair has no definite quantifier. title: The fixed-topology Polyakov metric integral
notes: Equation (5) uses maps \(x(\xi)\), an independent positive metric \(g\), a Gaussian kinetic action and the area term \(\mu_0^2\int\sqrt g\); the topology is explicitly fixed.
statement: For a fixed oriented surface \(\Sigma\), the formal bosonic-string action is \(S[x,g]=\frac12\int_\Sigma |dx|_g^2\,dA_g+\mu_0^2\int_\Sigma dA_g\). Maps and metrics are integrated modulo the chosen diffeomorphism gauge; conformal anomaly and metric moduli remain part of the definition. Equality with a combinatorial sum over embedded surfaces requires a regulator and a scaling-limit theorem, neither specified here.

fate: \citet[Eqs.~(3)--(10)]{polyakov1981quantum}, published 23 July 1981, gives this metric-integral formulation. The notebook reports an existing formal construction, not an established equality of all possible random-surface measures.

title: Functional metrics and the trace direction
notes: Equation (6) gives \(\|\delta x\|^2=\int\sqrt g\,|\delta x|^2\) and \(\|\delta g\|^2=\int\sqrt g\,(g^{aa\prime}g^{bb\prime}+c\,g^{ab}g^{a\prime b\prime})\delta g_{ab}\delta g_{a\prime b\prime}\).
statement: For a symmetric variation \(h\) of a two-dimensional positive metric, write \(h=h_0+\frac12(\operatorname{tr}_g h)g\). The second integrand equals \(|h_0|_g^2+(c+\frac12)(\operatorname{tr}_g h)^2\). It defines a positive inner product on all metric variations exactly when \(c>-\frac12\); equality is degenerate and smaller values give an indefinite trace direction.
reconstruction: The omitted condition on c is supplied. A positive field-space norm still does not create a countably additive flat volume measure.
fate: The invariant functional-metric prescription is in \citet[Eqs.~(6)--(10)]{polyakov1981quantum}. The positivity condition follows by the displayed trace decomposition, an elementary check \ours.

title: Diffeomorphisms and the covector connection sign
notes:
Equation (7) gives \(\delta g_{ab}=
abla_a\varepsilon_b+
abla_b\varepsilon_a\), but defines \(
abla_a\varepsilon_b=\partial_a\varepsilon_b+\Gamma^c_{ab}\varepsilon_c\).
statement:
For the Levi--Civita Christoffel symbols, a covector satisfies \(
abla_a\varepsilon_b=\partial_a\varepsilon_b-\Gamma^c_{ab}\varepsilon_c\). With \(\varepsilon_b=g_{bc}\varepsilon^c\), the metric Lie derivative is \((\mathcal L_\varepsilon g)_{ab}=
abla_a\varepsilon_b+

reconstruction: The usual Levi--Civita convention is fixed; the inverse coordinate-change convention could reverse the whole Lie derivative, but not only its Christoffel term.

title: Does dividing by gauge volume define the measure?
notes: After \(d\mu(x,g)=\mathcal Dx\,\mathcal Dg/\mathcal D\omega\), the notes say \ru{Теперь интеграл (5) определён хорошо}.
statement: Functional metrics and a formal quotient are not by themselves a measure construction. One must control a regulator, zero modes, gauge stabilizers, renormalization and metric moduli. A precise later result is the construction of spacelike Liouville correlation functions on the sphere for \(0<\gamma<2\), \(\mu>0\), \(Q=2/\gamma+\gamma/2\), and insertions satisfying \(\alpha_i<Q\), \(\sum_i\alpha_i>2Q\). This is a specified model, not the unrestricted quotient integral.
reconstruction: The later theorem is stated separately from the 1982 formal claim.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.2 and Definition~3.6]{davidkupiainenrhodesvargas2016liouville}, first circulated 27 October 2014 and published in 2016, gives the indicated rigorous construction. The bare uninserted sphere integral has a divergent zero-mode direction; the notebook\textquotesingle s assertion is not justified by (6)--(9).
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated subcritical sphere theory is constructed. The notes do not define a universal measure problem beyond that scope.

title: Conformal gauge, residual automorphisms and moduli
notes: The representative is \(g_{ab}=\rho\,\delta_{ab}\), followed by \ru{Остаётся конформная группа (конечномерная)}.
statement: Every smooth two-dimensional metric is locally conformally flat. Globally write \(g=e^\varphi\widehat g(m)\) using a reference metric in its conformal class and its moduli \(m\). For a fixed compact Riemann surface the global conformal automorphism group is finite-dimensional; germs of local conformal transformations are not. A single globally Euclidean chart does not cover an arbitrary closed surface.
reconstruction: The distinction between local coordinates, global automorphisms and moduli is added.
fate: \citet[Eqs.~(11)--(12) and discussion of moduli]{polyakov1981quantum} uses conformal gauge with global qualifications. The later sphere construction \citet[Section~3.2]{davidkupiainenrhodesvargas2016liouville} treats the residual Möbius action explicitly.

title: Matter and ghost determinants are different operators
notes: After Gaussian integration the notes say the determinants are identical and write \([\det\Delta_g]^{(26-d)/2}\) in equation (11).
statement: Writing \(\Delta_g\) for the nonnegative scalar Laplacian, integrating \(d\) scalar matter fields gives a factor \((\det{}^{\prime}\Delta_g)^{-d/2}\), with the translation zero modes treated separately. Gauge fixing contributes the determinant of the vector-to-traceless-tensor operator \(P\varepsilon=\nabla\varepsilon+(\nabla\varepsilon)^t-g\,\operatorname{div}\varepsilon\), together with zero-mode and moduli factors. The ghost conformal anomaly has coefficient \(-26\); it is not an exact identity of its determinant with the thirteenth power of the scalar Laplacian determinant.
reconstruction: Primed determinants and the actual ghost operator replace the literal scalar-determinant identification.
fate: \citet[Eqs.~(13)--(24)]{polyakov1981quantum} distinguishes the operators before calculating their conformal variations. Equation (11) captures an anomaly coefficient while suppressing determinant-line, zero-mode and global factors.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: The induced Liouville action and its scope
notes: Equation (12) sets \(\rho=e^\varphi\) and display the exponent \((d-26)S_L/(48\pi)\), with \(S_L=\int[\frac12(\partial\varphi)^2+m^2e^\varphi]\,d^2\xi\).
statement: The Weyl-anomaly calculation induces a local kinetic term for the conformal factor and a renormalized area term. On a curved reference surface it also includes a background-curvature coupling. The rigorous subcritical spacelike normalization uses a renormalized exponential, \(Q=2/\gamma+\gamma/2\), and central charge \(c_L=1+6Q^2>25\). Cancellation with matter requires \(c_{\mathrm m}+c_L-26=0\); this regime corresponds to \(c_{\mathrm m}<1\), not every integer target dimension \(d<26\).
reconstruction: The curved-background term, quantum renormalization and restricted matter-charge range are modern qualifications.
fate: The formal induced action was already in \citet[Eqs.~(25)--(31)]{polyakov1981quantum}. The quantum parameter shift and rigorous Weyl anomaly are verified in \citet[Introduction and Theorem~3.11]{davidkupiainenrhodesvargas2016liouville}. These later results clarify a specified branch without turning the notebook\textquotesingle s formal expression into a theorem for all dimensions.
present_status: As of November 2026: the formal anomaly mechanism is established, and the stated spacelike sphere realization is rigorous; no blanket all-dimension claim is made.

title: The field-dependent norm of the conformal factor
notes: Equation (13) gives \(\|\delta\varphi\|^2=\int e^\varphi(\delta\varphi)^2\,d^2\xi\) as the metric behind \(d\mu(\varphi)\).
statement: For \(g=e^\varphi\widehat g\), the induced trace-variation norm is proportional to \(\int_\Sigma e^\varphi(\delta\varphi)^2dA_{\widehat g}\), with a positive proportionality factor depending on the trace coefficient in (6). It is a field-dependent formal \(L^2\) metric. Its associated symbolic volume must not be replaced by flat \(\mathcal D\varphi\) without calculating a regulator-dependent Jacobian.

fate: \citet[Eqs.~(29)--(31)]{polyakov1981quantum} explicitly retains this nontrivial metric in the Liouville integral. Modern probabilistic constructions begin from a Gaussian free field and renormalized multiplicative chaos instead of a literal Riemannian volume in infinitely many dimensions.

title: The characteristic foliation and regular symplectic reduction
notes: \(X\) is complex, \(\Sigma\subset T^*X\) is conic and coisotropic, and \(\Sigma\to X\) is a fibration. The kernel of the restricted symplectic form is said to be integrable; its quotient \(M\) is assumed to be a fibration.
statement: For a smooth coisotropic \(\Sigma\) in a symplectic manifold \((P,\omega)\), \(\ker(\omega|_\Sigma)=(T\Sigma)^\omega\) is integrable. If its leaf space \(M\) is smooth and the quotient \(q:\Sigma\to M\) is a surjective submersion with connected fibers, there is a unique symplectic form \(\omega_M\) satisfying \(q^*\omega_M=\omega|_\Sigma\). Closed leaves alone do not guarantee a smooth Hausdorff quotient.
reconstruction: Smoothness and the quotient-submersion hypothesis are made explicit; the closed-form/Frobenius argument is the standard qualification.
fate: The notes expressly attribute the framework to earlier Guillemin--Sternberg work. \citet[Theorem~1]{ginzburg1983symplectic} uses the same characteristic reduction; its reference~3 records the author\textquotesingle s 1981 preprint. The 1983 publication date therefore cannot establish novelty in October 1982.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: The Lagrangian equivalence relation of a coisotropic quotient
notes: \(\Lambda=\{(\xi_1,\xi_2)\in\Sigma^2:\xi_1\sim\xi_2\}\) is Lagrangian and satisfies \(\Lambda^t=\Lambda\), \(\Lambda\circ\Lambda=\Lambda\).
statement: With the preceding regular quotient, \(\Lambda=\Sigma\times_M\Sigma\) is Lagrangian in \(P\times\overline P\), where the second symplectic form is \(-\omega\). If \(\dim P=2n\) and \(\operatorname{codim}\Sigma=k\), then \(\dim\Lambda=2n\); equality of the two pullbacks of \(q^*\omega_M\) gives isotropy. Symmetry and idempotence are the ordinary equivalence-relation identities.
reconstruction: The reversed symplectic sign and the regular fiber product are essential additions.
fate: This is the canonical-relation form of the reduction used in \citet[Section~2]{ginzburg1983symplectic}. The dimension and pullback check above is supplied explicitly \ours; the source does not present it as a new 1983 theorem.

title: The proposed converse for symmetric idempotent relations
notes: \ru{По-видимому, обратно}: a Lagrangian \(\Lambda\) with \(\Lambda^t=\Lambda\) and \(\Lambda\circ\Lambda=\Lambda\) should arise from \(\Sigma\).
statement: Under regularity assumptions on both projections, a smooth support \(\Sigma\), a smooth quotient and connected equivalence classes, the relation is the characteristic-leaf relation of a coisotropic support. The notebook does not say whether singular supports, immersed relations, disconnected classes or non-Hausdorff quotients are allowed, so an unrestricted global converse is not a uniquely specified assertion.

title: When Fourier integral kernels form an algebra
notes: Fourier integral operators associated with \(\Lambda\) are denoted \(\mathcal E_\Lambda\); they form a ring because \(\Lambda\circ\Lambda=\Lambda\).
statement: Closure under composition requires an admissible operator class: appropriate proper support, a clean canonical fiber product and the corresponding excess/order convention. In the transverse case, properly supported Fourier integral operators compose with summed orders when the canonical projection is proper. An idempotent set-theoretic relation alone does not ensure that arbitrary distribution kernels can be multiplied and integrated.
reconstruction: Support, cleanliness and filtration qualifications are supplied, without identifying the notation with a unique sheaf of microdifferential operators.
fate: The preexisting transverse theorem is \citet[Theorems~4.2.2--4.2.3]{hormander1971fourier}, published in 1971. The notebook\textquotesingle s characteristic quotient generally calls for its clean-composition extension; it does not specify a complete analytic or complex-microlocal calculus.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: The product model: pseudodifferential in one factor, smoothing in the other
notes: For \(X=X_1\times X_2\), the formula is \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(T^*X_1)\times0\); operators are pseudodifferential in \(X_1\), smoothing in \(X_2\). The preceding prose describes covectors normal to \(X_1\), along \(X_2\).
statement: The formula and operator description agree with \(\Sigma=T^*X_1\times0_{X_2}\): its covectors annihilate tangent vectors to the \(X_2\) fibers. Its characteristic leaves vary in \(X_2\), and \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(T^*X_1)\times(0_{X_2}\times0_{X_2})\). Here each zero denotes an entire zero section, not a single zero covector at one base point. Product kernels are pseudodifferential in the first variables and smooth in both second-factor variables.
reconstruction: The zero sections are expanded and the normal-direction wording is emended to match the two independent displayed descriptions.
fate: The distinction follows directly from the conormal and kernel definitions in \citet[Chapters~II--III]{hormander1971fourier}. The two factor labels in the notebook\textquotesingle s verbal normal-direction description are reversed relative to its formula and operator conclusion.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Shmelyov’s conormal embedding condition
notes: Shmelyov draws a double fibration \(Z\to X,Y\) and requires the induced map \(N^*Z\to T^*Y\) to be an embedding.
statement: For a smooth incidence submanifold \(Z\subset X\times Y\), remove zero covectors and use the signed conormal as the canonical relation of the integral transform \(R:C_c^\infty(X)\to C^\infty(Y)\). Injective immersion of its projection to the data cotangent bundle is the Bolker condition. With appropriate properness and a nonvanishing weight, \(R^*R\) is pseudodifferential and elliptic on visible covectors; complete visibility gives global microlocal ellipticity. This alone does not imply exact injectivity for every smooth weight.
reconstruction: The incidence embedding, zero-section removal, signs, properness and visibility are specified.
fate: \citet[Introduction and Section~2]{homanzhou2017radon} explicitly attributes the FIO and Bolker normal-operator theorem to earlier Guillemin--Sternberg work. Its modern injectivity and stability theorems impose additional analytic or generic hypotheses. Thus the condition in the notes is expository; later stronger results are kept separate.

title: The massless Yang–Mills–Higgs energy and magnetic charge
notes: For \(SU(2)\) with a three-component adjoint scalar, \(E=\int(|D_A\varphi|^2+F^2)\,dx\) on \(\mathbb R^3\). A monopole has \(\deg(\varphi|_{S^2_\infty})=1\); minimum-energy solutions are known.
statement: Choose a positive invariant inner product on \(\mathfrak{su}_2\), coupling one, finite energy and \(|\Phi|\to v>0\). The normalized asymptotic Higgs field defines \(k=\deg(\Phi/|\Phi|:S^2_\infty\to S^2)\). For \(E=\frac12\int(|B|^2+|D_A\Phi|^2)\), square completion gives \(E\ge4\pi v|k|\), attained by \(B=\pm D_A\Phi\). The absent Higgs potential identifies the Prasad--Sommerfield limit.
reconstruction: Asymptotic norm, positive inner product, factor one-half and magnetic field notation are added.
fate: This is the older Bogomolny framework underlying \citet[abstract and setup]{taubes1982nonminimal1}. The square completion fixes the normalization; no claim that every minimizer is explicitly produced by twistors is needed.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Nonminimal stationary points and the monopole–antimonopole minimax
notes: After the charge-one definition the notes ask for other stationary points, answer yes, cite Taubes, draw a noncontractible loop and compare the solution with a monopole--antimonopole pair. The displayed maximum and minimum are reversed.
statement: Does the finite-energy \(SU(2)\) Yang--Mills--Higgs functional in the massless-Higgs limit have critical points outside both Bogomolny equations? The loop method seeks \(c=\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\sup_{t\in S^1}E(\gamma(t))\), with \(\Gamma\) a fixed nontrivial loop class in the gauge quotient and compactness proved separately. A monopole--antimonopole pair has total charge zero; it does not itself answer a fixed charge-one question.
reconstruction: The definite existence question is separated from the ambiguous fixed-sector reading; the variational order is emended.
fate: \citet[abstract]{taubes1982nonminimal2} published existence in September 1982, before this talk. The later each-sector multiplicity theorem \citep{taubes1985minmax} requires the corrected argument in \citet{taubes1989erratum}. These papers were checked at publisher-abstract and metadata level.
present_status: As of November 2026: nonminimal finite-energy solutions are established in this massless-Higgs model; sector details are not inferred from the pair picture.

title: A unit instanton on a simply connected homology four-sphere
notes: For compact \(M^4\) with \(\pi_1(M)=1\), \(H^2(M)=0\), and a conformal structure, is there an \(SU(2)\) connection with \(F=\pm *F\) and characteristic class one? The answer is yes, citing Taubes, CMP 1981.
statement: For a smooth closed oriented simply connected four-manifold with \(H^2(M;\mathbb R)=0\) and a smooth metric, the charge-one \(SU(2)\) bundle admits an anti-self-dual connection. Equivalently reverse orientation and use self-duality with \(c_2[M]=-1\). The Hodge star on two-forms is conformally invariant.
reconstruction: Closedness, smoothness, orientation, coefficients and the charge/self-duality sign are specified.
fate: Taubes existence is invoked explicitly in \citet[Section~3, reference~6]{donaldson1983selfdual}. The identifiable original is JDG 17 (1982), 139--170, rather than CMP 1981. Verification is indirect through Donaldson; the original full proof was inaccessible.
present_status: As of November 2026: existence is established; an instanton does not identify the manifold diffeomorphically with the standard sphere.

title: The five-dimensional instanton moduli calculation
notes: The parameter space is a five-dimensional manifold, as for the sphere.
statement: The charge-one anti-self-dual complex has virtual real dimension \(8-3(1-b_1+b_2^+)=5\). The moduli space is smooth of this dimension near irreducible unobstructed connections. A suitable generic perturbation gives regularity; the index alone does not give a smooth moduli space for every unperturbed metric.
reconstruction: Virtual dimension, actual regularity and stabilizers are distinguished.
fate: \citet[Lemma~1]{donaldson1983selfdual} supplies generic perturbation, using the earlier Atiyah--Hitchin--Singer dimension formula.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: The instanton end and a five-dimensional cobordism
notes: The parameter space \(B\) has boundary diffeomorphic to \(M^4\).
statement: The charge-one moduli space has a bubbling end parametrized by concentration point and scale, \(M\times(0,\varepsilon)\). After regular perturbation and compactification, absence of reducibles in the \(H^2=0\) case yields a compact oriented five-manifold with boundary \(M\). The boundary is not already contained in the smooth space of connections.
reconstruction: Bubbling compactification and perturbation are restored.
fate: \citet[Lemma~2]{donaldson1983selfdual} gives the product end and compact complement. Received 9 August 1982, published January 1983; an exact earlier public circulation date was not found.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: Oriented four-dimensional cobordism and the signature
notes: \(M^4\) is a boundary iff its Pontryagin class vanishes, equivalently its intersection-form signature vanishes.
statement: For smooth closed oriented \(M^4\), oriented null-cobordism is equivalent to \(\sigma(M)=0\), or \(\langle p_1(TM),[M]\rangle=0\). Indeed \(\Omega_4^{SO}\simeq\mathbb Z\), generated by \(\mathbb{CP}^2\), and \(\langle p_1,[M]\rangle=3\sigma(M)\). For connected oriented \(M\), the number also detects the top-degree integral class.
reconstruction: Oriented cobordism and the characteristic number specify the shorthand.
fate: This is old material: \citet[Theorem~IV.13 and Corollary~IV.14]{thom1954globales}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Donaldson’s diagonalization theorem versus a manifold classification
notes: A positive-definite form implies that the manifold is an \ru{обобщ. проект. плоск. \(CP^2\)}; hence its integral form is a sum of squares.
statement: If \(M\) is smooth, closed, oriented and simply connected with positive-definite intersection form, then \(Q_M\simeq_{\mathbb Z}\operatorname{diag}(1,\ldots,1)\). The theorem does not assert \(M\cong\#_{b_2}\mathbb{CP}^2\) by diffeomorphism.
reconstruction: The conclusion is restricted to integral forms.
fate: The exact conclusion is \citet[Theorem, p.~81]{donaldson1983selfdual}. Fröhlich reports Donaldson; the manifold-equality wording exceeds that theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: Reducible instantons and cones on the complex projective plane
notes: For the positive-definite case, \(B\) has singularities that are cones over \(\mathbb{CP}^2\).
statement: In this charge-one self-dual problem, suitable perturbations leave isolated reducibles modeled on \(\mathbb C^3/S^1=C(\mathbb{CP}^2)\). Their number is \(n(Q)=\frac12\#\{a:Q(a)=1\}\). Removing cone neighborhoods gives a cobordism between \(M\) and \(n(Q)\) projective planes; signature and the norm-one-vector bound force diagonalization.
reconstruction: Charge, regularity, reducibility and the lattice count are supplied.
fate: The local model and count appear in \citet[Sections~3--4]{donaldson1983selfdual}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: The weak Morse inequalities and their hypotheses
notes: For isolated critical points, \(M_p\) counts points with \(p\) negative Hessian eigenvalues; \(M_p\ge B_p\).
statement: For a smooth Morse function on a smooth closed manifold, let \(m_p\) count its nondegenerate critical points of index \(p\). Then \(m_p\ge b_p(M;\mathbb R)\). Isolated degenerate critical points cannot in general be counted solely by their negative Hessian eigenvalues.
reconstruction: Closedness and nondegeneracy are restored.
fate: These classical inequalities are the starting point of \citet[Section~2]{witten1982supersymmetry}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Conjugating the de Rham differential
notes: \(d_t=e^{-tf}de^{tf}\), \(d_t^2=0\), and unchanged cohomology are followed by \(d_t=d-t\,df\wedge\).
statement: The conjugation gives \(d_t=d+t\,df\wedge\), \(d_t^*=d^*+t\,\iota_{\nabla f}\). Multiplication by \(e^{tf}\) is a chain isomorphism \((\Omega^*,d_t)\to(\Omega^*,d)\), proving nilpotence and unchanged cohomology. The two later minuses instead correspond to \(t\mapsto-t\).
reconstruction: The consistent sign and chain isomorphism replace the loose appeal to homotopy.
fate: See \citet[Section~2, equations~(9)--(10)]{witten1982supersymmetry}. Received 26 March 1982, published December 1982; receipt is not a verified public-preprint date.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: Deformed Hodge representatives
notes: Representatives satisfy \(d_t\omega=0\) and \((\omega,d_t\beta)=0\), hence \(\Box_t\omega=0\).
statement: On a closed Riemannian manifold, \(\Delta_t=d_t^*d_t+d_td_t^*\) is nonnegative self-adjoint elliptic, with \(\langle\Delta_t\omega,\omega\rangle=\|d_t\omega\|^2+\|d_t^*\omega\|^2\). Deformed harmonic forms represent its cohomology, so \(\dim\ker(\Delta_t|_{\Omega^p})=b_p\) for every finite \(t\).
reconstruction: Compactness and the analytic operator setting are explicit.
fate: This is the Hodge step in \citet[Section~2, equation~(11)]{witten1982supersymmetry}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: Exterior algebra as a fermionic Fock space
notes: Kirillov identifies \(a_i\) with contraction and \(a_i^*\) with exterior multiplication, correcting the initial description of \(a_i\). The mixed anticommutator is \(\delta_{ij}\), and \(a_i\Omega_0=0\).
statement: For an orthonormal one-particle basis, \(\mathcal F_-=\Lambda^*\mathbb C^n\), \(a_i^*=e_i\wedge\), \(a_i=\iota_{e_i}\), \(\Omega_0=1\). Besides \(\{a_i,a_j^*\}=\delta_{ij}\), one has \(\{a_i,a_j\}=\{a_i^*,a_j^*\}=0\). Ordered creation products form the exterior basis; an unrestricted antisymmetric coefficient sum requires a matching factorial convention.
reconstruction: The omitted anticommutators and coefficient convention are supplied.
fate: The standard fermionic algebra is recalled in \citet[Section~2, before equation~(13)]{witten1982supersymmetry}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.
speaker: A. A. Kirillov and Jürgen Fröhlich

title: The Witten Laplacian and its Hessian term
notes: \(\Box_t=\Box+t^2(df)^2+t\sum[a_i^*,a_j]\partial_i\partial_jf\).
statement: For the plus-sign differential, in an orthonormal frame, \[\Delta_t=\Delta+t^2|df|^2+t\sum_{i,j}(\nabla^2f)_{ij}[a_i^*,a_j].\] The Hessian is covariant. On functions its last term is \(-t\operatorname{tr}(\nabla^2f)\), independently checked by applying \(d_t^*d_t\).
reconstruction: Covariant derivatives and the nonnegative Laplacian convention are restored.
fate: Compare \citet[Section~2, equation~(13)]{witten1982supersymmetry}. The zero-form check is supplied here \ours.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: The normal harmonic oscillator at a Morse point
notes: For \(f=f_0+\sum s_i\lambda_i y_i^2+O(|y|^3)\), the potential is \(4t^2\sum\lambda_i^2y_i^2\), but the Hessian sum uses \(i<j\) and marginal factors four.
statement: For \(\lambda_i>0\), \(s_i=\pm1\), the quadratic model is \[H_t^{\rm quad}=\sum_i(-\partial_{y_i}^2+4t^2\lambda_i^2y_i^2)+2t\sum_i s_i\lambda_i[a_i^*,a_i].\] The Hessian has diagonal entries \(2s_i\lambda_i\); restricting to \(i<j\) loses them all. Since \([a_i^*,a_i]=2N_i-1\), the bosonic ground energy cancels for occupation \(N_i=0\) in positive directions and \(N_i=1\) in negative directions.
reconstruction: Diagonal terms and their coefficient are emended.
fate: See \citet[Section~2, equations~(15)--(18)]{witten1982supersymmetry}. The notebook normalization gives the factor two, independently checked \ours.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: The missing Gaussian in the local ground state
notes: The operator allegedly annihilates \(dy_{n-p+1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dy_n\).
statement: The unique square-integrable zero mode of the quadratic model, up to scalar, is \[\omega_{0,t}=e^{-t\sum_i\lambda_i y_i^2}dy_{n-p+1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dy_n.\] The bare wedge is neither annihilated nor square-integrable on \(\mathbb R^n\). Direct differentiation verifies \(H_t^{\rm quad}\omega_{0,t}=0\); all other oscillator/Fock occupations have positive energy.
reconstruction: The scalar Gaussian is an essential emendation.
fate: The degree selection matches \citet[Section~2, equation~(18)]{witten1982supersymmetry}. The Gaussian substitution is checked here \ours.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: Small eigenvalues, quasimodes and the Morse inequalities
notes: The notes explicitly seek small rather than necessarily zero eigenvalues; each critical point gives an approximate eigenfunction.
statement: On a closed manifold with Morse \(f\), for large \(t\) the low-energy spectral subspace of \(\Delta_t\) in degree \(p\) has dimension \(m_p\), containing the \(b_p\)-dimensional kernel. Cut-off local Gaussians are quasimodes; their small eigenvalues need not vanish. The low-energy subcomplex yields strong and weak Morse inequalities.
reconstruction: A spectral cutoff, the large-parameter regime and the subcomplex make the shorthand precise.
fate: \citet[Section~2]{witten1982supersymmetry} presents the semiclassical mechanism. Its original asymptotic argument is distinguished from a complete modern analytic proof.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: Gelfand’s replacement of cycle modifications by form modifications
notes: Gelfand says \ru{вместо перестроек в циклах --- перестройки в формах}, connecting differential operators with Morse modifications.
statement: The remark describes the passage from handle attachments and cycles to spectral localization of the de Rham complex near critical points. It proposes no theorem beyond the surrounding construction.

present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Supersymmetry as geometry of field configurations
notes: \(d_t\) is a supercharge; an expression with \(\delta/\delta\varphi(x)\) and \(ta^*(x)\varphi^n(x)\) is compared with \(d+t\,df\wedge\). In two dimensions fermions are forms on bosonic configuration space.
statement: Finite-dimensional supersymmetric quantum mechanics uses \(d_t,d_t^*\). For a theory on a spatial circle, the analogous configuration space is a space of maps. The form picture is formal until domains, a measure and regularized operators are specified. The functional derivative displayed in the notes alone does not define a quantum field operator.

title: The proposed higher-dimensional gauge-field interpretation
notes: For \(d>2\), gauge fields may be needed for an analogous interpretation, which is unavailable. A parenthesis calls the Poincaré group \ru{простая}.
statement: No supersymmetry algebra, target, signature, gauge group or proposed complex is specified, so no single unresolved problem is determined. If \ru{простая} means algebraically simple, it is false because translations form a proper normal subgroup; in context it may mean uncomplicated.

title: Enss’s announcement of three-body Coulomb asymptotic completeness
notes: Enss is credited with asymptotic completeness for three particles with Coulomb interaction.
statement: For three nonrelativistic particles in \(\mathbb R^3\) with positive finite masses and pair Coulomb potentials, after removing center-of-mass motion, the modified channel wave operators exist and their orthogonal ranges exhaust the continuous spectral subspace. Channels include three separated particles and each bound pair plus a third particle. Long-range Dollard modifiers account for Coulomb phases.
reconstruction: Quantum mechanics, channel projections and long-range comparison dynamics are supplied.

The precise 1982 announced version was not located.
