title: Four motivations for statistical mechanics of surfaces
notes: Applications listed are crystal growth, phase interfaces, lattice gauge theories and dual-resonance strings.
statement: These motivate different ensembles: height graphs approximate interfaces, gauge expansions produce plaquette configurations, and string functional integrals sum over maps and metrics. Sharing a surface interpretation does not identify their measures or critical exponents.
fate: The same four motivations appear in \citet[Introduction]{frohlichpfisterspencer1982surfaces}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: The solid-on-solid measure with zero boundary heights
notes: For finite \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^2\), \(h_p\in\mathbb Z\), \(h_p=0\) outside, add vertical walls and use \(e^{-\beta\operatorname{area}(S)}=e^{-\beta|\Lambda|}\prod_{\langle p,q\rangle}e^{-\beta|h_p-h_q|}\).
statement: Let \(\mathcal H_\Lambda=\{h:\mathbb Z^2\to\mathbb Z:h=0\text{ outside }\Lambda\}\). Sum each unordered nearest-neighbor edge meeting \(\Lambda\) once and set \(H_\Lambda(h)=\sum_{\langle p,q\rangle}|h_p-h_q|\). For \(\beta>0\), \(Z_\Lambda=\sum_h e^{-\beta H_\Lambda(h)}<\infty\), and \(\mu_{\Lambda,\beta}=Z_\Lambda^{-1}e^{-\beta H_\Lambda}\). The constant horizontal area cancels in normalization; this model excludes overhangs.
reconstruction: The bond-counting convention and finite-volume state space are explicit.
fate: Compare \citet[Section~7, equation~(7.16)]{frohlichspencer1981transition}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Localization and exponential height tails at large inverse temperature
notes: For large \(\beta\), \(\mathbb E h_p^2\) is bounded and \(\Pr(|h_p|=n)\sim e^{-{\rm const}\,n}\), attributed to Dobrushin.
statement: For sufficiently large \(\beta\), zero-boundary SOS measures satisfy a volume-uniform bound \(\Pr(|h_p|\ge n)\le C_\beta e^{-c_\beta n}\), hence \(\sup_{\Lambda,p}\mathbb E h_p^2<\infty\). A Peierls contour argument proves such exponential bounds; the displayed \(\sim\) is not by itself a verified sharp tail asymptotic.
reconstruction: An exponential bound replaces an unsupported asymptotic equivalence; the finite-volume zero-boundary convention is retained.
fate: \citet[Section~7, Remark~2 after Theorem~7.3]{frohlichspencer1981transition} recalls the low-temperature argument. The notebook attribution to Dobrushin is broader than the exact SOS proof identified here.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Logarithmic height-difference fluctuations at small inverse temperature
notes: For small \(\beta\), \(c_2\log(1+|p-q|)\le\mathbb E(h_p-h_q)^2\le c_1\log(1+|p-q|)\).
statement: In a thermodynamic gradient-state limit of the two-dimensional SOS model, for sufficiently small \(\beta>0\) there are positive finite \(c_-(\beta),c_+(\beta)\) bounding \(\mathbb E(h_p-h_q)^2\) above and below by the corresponding multiples of \(\log(1+|p-q|)\). This is a statement about differences; unpinned absolute heights need not have a finite-variance infinite-volume law.
reconstruction: Gradient limits, coupling-dependent constants and the distinction between absolute and relative heights are stated.
fate: The lower bound is \citet[Theorem~7.3 and equation~(7.18)]{frohlichspencer1981transition}; the matching upper bound is recorded in \citet[Theorem~4(2)]{frohlichpfisterspencer1982surfaces}. The 1981 publication predates this talk.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: Microscopic height shifts versus an enhanced continuous symmetry
notes: The product weight is said to have continuous symmetry \(h_p\mapsto h_p+\mathrm{const}\), broken by the boundary condition, and to gain symmetry on shrinking the squares.
statement: For integer-valued heights the exact global shifts are \(h\mapsto h+k\), \(k\in\mathbb Z\); zero boundary values break even this action on a fixed finite-volume state space. Real shifts occur in a continuous-field representation or a scaling description, not as transformations of the original integer configurations. A scaling-limit claim additionally needs an observable topology and rescaling prescription.
reconstruction: The discrete symmetry and the formal enhanced symmetry are separated.
fate: \citet[Section~2, equations~(28)--(29)]{frohlichpfisterspencer1982surfaces} puts the real shift symmetry in a renormalized continuous-field representation.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: The passage from height graphs to general plaquette surfaces
notes: \(Z_{\beta,\gamma}=\sum_{\partial S=\gamma}e^{-\beta|S|}\), and the analogous small-\(\beta\) questions are said not to be done.
statement: To define a finite count, specify connected surfaces attached to a fixed finite boundary \(\gamma\), the ambient lattice, permitted intersections, plaquette multiplicities and topology. If disconnected components can be placed arbitrarily far away, even a fixed-area count can be infinite. Connected sets with each plaquette used at most once have at most exponential counting growth, by bounded-degree lattice-animal enumeration.
reconstruction: Connectedness and multiplicity restrictions are necessary editorial qualifications; no unique general ensemble is silently selected.
fate: \citet[Section~3, ensembles (a)--(c)]{frohlichpfisterspencer1982surfaces} explicitly distinguishes the alternatives. Its SOS theorem does not apply to all of them.
present_status: As of November 2026: the qualified statement is established; the notebook is an exposition, not a newly open question.

title: The asserted exponential times power counting asymptotic
notes: \(a_\gamma(n)=\#\{S:\partial S=\gamma,|S|=n\}\sim C_\gamma^n n^{\delta(\gamma)}\), allegedly from general combinatorial theorems.
statement: An exponential growth rate, where established, means \(\log a_\gamma(n)=n\log C+o(n)\) along admissible area values. It does not imply a polynomial prefactor: for example \(a_n=\lfloor C^ne^{\sqrt n}\rfloor\) has the same exponential rate and no form \(A C^n n^\delta\). The notebook does not fix the surface class or area periodicity needed for the stronger claim.
reconstruction: The verified leading growth is separated from the unverified power-law refinement.
fate: \citet[abstract]{durhuusfrohlichjonsson1983surfaces} states only exponential growth with an \(o(n)\) remainder for its two specified models. The counterexample to the inference is an elementary check \ours.
present_status: As of November 2026: the quoted general-combinatorics justification does not establish the displayed asymptotic; its exact model-dependent version is not determined by the notes.

title: Boundary independence of the exponential growth rate
notes: The limit \(n^{-1}\log a_\gamma(n)\) is introduced and \(C_\gamma\) is asserted independent of \(\gamma\).
statement: For the self-avoiding and planar random-surface models considered by Durhuus--Fröhlich--Jónsson, the admissible-area growth satisfies \(a_\gamma(n)=\exp(\beta_0n+o(n))\), with \(\beta_0\) independent of the fixed admissible boundary. A finite boundary modification explains the mechanism, but it must preserve the chosen surface class; it is not a theorem about every object called a surface.
reconstruction: The theorem is restricted to the identified models and admissible areas.
fate: \citet[abstract]{durhuusfrohlichjonsson1983surfaces} is a direct later match, published 31 October 1983 with the speaker as coauthor. Exact preprint date and full proof were not verified.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identification and limits are as stated above.

title: Does the subexponential exponent depend only on boundary topology?
notes: \(\delta(\gamma)\) should depend on topological properties of \(\gamma\); sketches contrast one and several boundary components.
statement: Once a particular asymptotic \(a_\gamma(n)\sim A_\gamma C^n n^{\delta_\gamma}\) and a surface ensemble are fixed, one can ask whether \(\delta_\gamma\) depends only on the number and knot/link type of boundary components, or also on genus restrictions and embedding dimension. The notes do not choose these parameters and do not establish existence of \(\delta_\gamma\).
fate: The exponential theorem in \citet{durhuusfrohlichjonsson1983surfaces} does not determine a power exponent. Searches of surface-counting and topology literature did not yield a theorem matching the unqualified conjecture.
present_status: As of November 2026: a universal topological exponent cannot be assigned without specifying the ensemble and proving that such an exponent exists.

title: The number of handles of a typical surface
notes: What happens when all topologies are allowed, and how many handles does a typical surface have?
statement: A typical genus requires a normalized probability measure: for example a fixed-area ensemble, or a grand-canonical ensemble with specified area and genus weights. It also requires a class of actual surfaces, since a branched plaquette complex need not have a manifold genus. None of the limiting regimes or weights is fixed at this question.

title: The partition-function abscissa from counting growth

title: The proposed edge-length measure and its scale divergence

title: Primary covariance does not uniquely define the field
notes: \([L_n,\varphi(z)]=z^{n+1}\varphi^{\prime}(z)+(n+1)\Delta z^n\varphi(z)\), followed by \ru{Он опрд. этой ф-лой однозначно}.
statement: In the modern convention, a primary field of weight \(\delta\) obeys \([\ell_n,\varphi(z)]=[z^{n+1}\partial_z+(n+1)\delta z^n]\varphi(z)\). title: Computing primary correlators and the role of null states
notes: The first question asks how to calculate \(\langle0|\varphi(z_1)\cdots\varphi(z_n)|0\rangle\).

title: The contravariant Gram form and positivity

statement: For real \(c,h\), these conditions determine the contravariant Hermitian form on the Verma module by moving positive modes to the right; for complex parameters use the algebraic bilinear form with the standard antiautomorphism. The form can be degenerate or indefinite. For example \(\|\ell_{-1}|h\rangle\|^2=2h\), so positivity does not follow for arbitrary \(h\). The radical is removed when forming the irreducible highest-weight quotient.

title: Neretin on reducibility and the first singular level
notes: Neretin gives a two-factor polynomial with \(-\Delta\) in both factors, then says degeneration occurs at level \(\alpha\beta\), for positive integers \(\alpha,\beta\).
statement: For the reverse Witt bracket of the notebook, set \(\ell_n=-L_n\) and \(h=-\Delta\). In the corresponding central normalization, write \(c=13-6(t+t^{-1})\), \(t\ne0\). Thus the recorded \(-\Delta\) is exactly \(h\), and its two-factor polynomial has the correct Kac form. At level two the Gram determinant is \(2h[16h^2+(2c-10)h+c]\): at \(c=0\), \(h=5/8\) corresponds to the recorded \(\Delta=-5/8\).

title: Critical dimension and the remaining worldsheet integrations

title: Liouville stationary states as Virasoro representations

title: The improved classical Liouville stress tensor
notes: The purported conserved traceless tensor ends with \(\alpha\varphi_{ab}-\beta\delta_{ab}(\partial\varphi)^2\); it has no potential or Laplacian improvement term.

title: Recovering Virasoro modes from the stress field
